data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The nocturnal UHI is primarily governed by aridity and regional wind speed, where dry, calm conditions maximize both thermal storage and the nocturnal gap by minimizing advective cooling and latent heat loss.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If regional wind speeds exceed the threshold for forced convection, the nocturnal heat island is rapidly flushed regardless of aridity.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If arid rural areas exhibit thermal storage and cooling rates identical to urban areas, the aridity mechanism does not explain a differential gap.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Aridity reduces soil moisture, decreasing rural evapotranspiration and latent heat cooling, but high imperviousness in cities still exacerbates sensible heat storage.
